headline: Australian Federal Police Charge Sydney Trader With Insider Trading on $2.4 Billion Takeover Deal
summary: The Australian Federal Police charged Marcus Chen, a 38-year-old equity trader at a Sydney investment firm, with insider trading related to a $2.4 billion corporate takeover announced in March 2026. Prosecutors allege Chen purchased 47,000 shares in the target company two weeks before the public announcement, profiting approximately $890,000. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission assisted in the 14-month investigation that examined trading records and communications across three financial institutions.
key_points: Marcus Chen faces criminal charges for allegedly purchasing 47,000 shares using non-public information about an upcoming $2.4 billion acquisition.
The Sydney trader reportedly gained $890,000 in profit from trades executed two weeks before the March 2026 takeover announcement.
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission conducted a 14-month investigation examining records across three financial institutions.
This marks the eighth insider trading prosecution brought by Australian Federal Police since new enforcement guidelines took effect in January 2025.
If convicted, Chen faces up to 10 years imprisonment and financial penalties of three times the profit obtained under Australian securities law.
